title: Two sinusoids make one
caption: 3 sin ωt and 4 cos ωt (thin curves) add to a single sinusoid of amplitude R = √(3² + 4²) = 5 (heavy curve), shifted by φ = 53.1° (tan φ = 4/3). The sum peaks at 5, as the worked example finds, at ωt = 0.644 rad.
alt: Graph over one cycle of 3 sin ωt, 4 cos ωt and their sum, a sine wave of amplitude 5 that peaks at ωt = 0.644 radians.
description: Horizontal axis: ωt in radians over one cycle, 0 to 2π; vertical axis: the value of each expression.
The thin curves are 3 sin ωt (amplitude 3) and 4 cos ωt (amplitude 4).
Their sum, the heavy curve, is again sinusoidal with amplitude R = √(3² + 4²) = 5 and phase φ = arctan(4/3) = 53.1°.
Its maximum is 5, reached when ωt + φ = π/2, that is at ωt = 0.644 rad.

checks.name: the maximum of 3 sin ωt + 4 cos ωt is 5
